name: Lake Tuz spring vs late summer 2021

confidence.note: LOWERED: 53% of the comparable area is very bright non-vegetated surface (salt, sand, snow or similar) where change detection is not reliable. Do not read the absence of change there as no change. Heuristic score from 0 to 1 (magnitude of the index change, number of valid observations, size). It is not a probability of being correct.

vegetation_loss_likely_cause.note: A hint from dNBR, brightness and shape, not a verdict on the cause. 'fire-like' does not prove a fire; 'clearing-like' covers felling, harvest, ploughing and construction.
sources: Key & Benson (2006) FIREMON Landscape Assessment: dNBR severity thresholds 0.10 / 0.27 / 0.44 / 0.66
Copernicus EFFIS fire severity (same thresholds applied to Sentinel-2): https://forest-fire.emergency.copernicus.eu/about-effis/technical-background/fire-severity
UN-SPIDER recommended practice: burn severity mapping with NBR / dNBR
vegetation_loss_likely_cause.own_thresholds: brightness and rectangularity thresholds are this project's heuristics, checked on only two public cases

bright_surface.rule: mean(blue, green, red) >= 0.25 and NDVI < 0.15 in the before or after composite (salt, sand, snow, bare limestone, concrete)

water_like_share_of_bright_pixels.index: NDWI = (green - NIR) / (green + NIR) > 0 (exploratory; the default MNDWI rule scores dry salt as water too)

reasons: the windows are 153 days apart in the seasonal cycle
53% of the area is very bright non-vegetated surface (salt, sand, snow): change there is not reliable
76% of the area is cloud-free in both periods
data_quality.note: Grades the data behind the comparison, not the correctness of the polygons; even 'good' is unverified by field data.

largest_areas.likely_cause_basis: dNBR 0.41 (at least moderate-low burn severity); irregular outline (rectangularity 0.35)
dNBR 0.33 (at least moderate-low burn severity); irregular outline (rectangularity 0.43); bright after (visible reflectance 0.23), like exposed soil or stubble

warnings: The two windows are 153 days apart in the seasonal cycle. Vegetation and water change naturally with the season: compare the same time of year in different years to avoid false alarms.

53% of the comparable area is very bright, non-vegetated surface (salt, sand, snow or similar; 28% in both periods). Change detection is NOT reliable on such surfaces: do not read the absence of change there as 'no change'. Confidence of polygons on bright pixels is lowered.

Exploratory signal on the bright surface: the share of water-like pixels (NDWI > 0) changed from 84% to 2%, which suggests a bright surface (a salt flat or shallow lake) became drier. The default MNDWI rule cannot see this because dry salt also scores as water in MNDWI. Not a mapped change: verify with other data.
backend: Element 84 Earth Search (Sentinel-2 L2A COGs on AWS Open Data)
present_to_user: The three images (before, after, detected changes) are returned with this result; refer to them.
Give hectares and polygon counts per class, the comparable share of the area, the confidence and the data quality, and EVERY warning above.

Say what the classes mean (a spectral change). likely_cause is only a hint from dNBR, brightness and shape: say 'fire-like' or 'clearing-like', never 'it was a fire'; drought, harvest and construction can look alike.
If seasonal_check is present, report the hectares flagged likely_seasonal (they repeat in earlier years, so probably harvest or a seasonal cycle); those polygons are kept.
If bright_surface.reliable is false, say that change on salt, sand or snow is not reliable and that no change there must not be read as no change; the confidence was lowered.
earthdiff is a screening tool: it flags where free Sentinel-2 imagery changed. It is not an official damage, burned-area, flood or deforestation assessment.
Credit the data: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2021.
